_notes: E4 R1.4: the seminary (systems/bishop/seminary.ts). Where the see's men are formed and what a year there grows in each pillar; what the bishop asks the rector to stress; the applicants' backgrounds, strengths, and the concerns formation surfaces; the rector's report lines; the ordination. Rates and growth are invented and flagged; the six years and the pillars follow the Program of Priestly Formation in outline (to verify).

own.label: The diocese's own seminary
own.blurb: The see has a major seminary of its own: the rector is yours to name, the faculty is your priests, and the men are formed among the parishes they will serve. It costs the diocese, and it forms men who know the diocese.

province.label: The province's seminary
province.blurb: A seminary two states away, shared with the province's dioceses: a rector you did not choose, a faculty you cannot touch, and a bill that arrives in August. The men come home in summer and are strangers for the rest of the year.

rome.label: Rome
rome.blurb: Every man to a Roman college: the pontifical university, the languages, the Church seen whole, and a diocese that gets back scholars who have not sat in a rectory in six years. Rome notices a see that sends its men.

human.label: Human formation
human.blurb: Men who can be lived with: the rectory, the office, the woman at the door. It surfaces the immaturity and the isolation early, when they can still be worked on.

spiritual.label: Spiritual formation
spiritual.blurb: The hour of prayer before the day, the director every month, the man's own doubt met before it meets a parish.

intellectual.label: Intellectual formation
intellectual.blurb: The theology done properly, the Latin kept, the men who can preach because they have read. It surfaces the rigid mind.

pastoral.label: Pastoral formation
pastoral.blurb: Summers in the parishes, the hospital, the prison, the funeral home. The men come to ordination already tired and already useful.

backgrounds: a farm boy from the north of the diocese
a convert of thirty with a law degree
the youngest of nine, an altar server since he could carry the book
a schoolteacher who left a classroom for the seminary at thirty-four
an engineer who prayed the rosary in the car for ten years before he told anyone
a graduate of the state university with a philosophy degree and a debt
a Mexican-American from the immigrant parish, the first vocation it has sent
a college athlete the Newman Center caught
a bookkeeper from the cathedral parish who has counted the collection for twelve years

strengths.text: prays like a man who means it
can talk to anyone, and does
has already buried his own parents and knows what a funeral is for
ran a Bible study of forty at the university
has a director's calm at twenty-four
is liked by old women and small children, which is the whole test

rigid.label: cannot be corrected
rigid.seen: The rector writes that the man is pious in a way that impresses the older pastors and cannot be corrected: not will not, cannot. A summer pastor has asked that he not return.

immature.label: not yet a man
immature.seen: The rector writes that the man is twenty-six going on seventeen: a good heart, no discipline, and a phone he cannot put down at table.

doubt.label: a doubt he has not named
doubt.seen: His director, without breaking anything, has let the rector know that the man is carrying a question about the faith that he has not put into words to anyone, and that the third year is the year such questions either get asked or get buried.

isolated.label: alone in a full house
isolated.seen: The rector writes that the man eats alone by choice, has made no friend in two years, and will be a lonely priest, which is the kind the diocese loses.

health.label: a health he does not mention
health.seen: The summer assignment ended early: a collapse in the sacristy that the pastor called heat and the doctor called something else. The man asked that you not be told.

drink.label: a taste for it
drink.seen: The rector writes, carefully, that the man's Saturday nights have been noticed by the house, and that the house has been told to stop noticing, and has not.

ambition.label: has read the ladder
ambition.seen: The rector writes that the man has asked twice which seminarians the bishop has met and whether Rome is possible, and that he preaches, already, for the back pew where the chancery sits.

human.low: a man the house finds hard to live with
human.middling: a man the house lives with
human.high: a man the house would follow

spiritual.low: a prayer life the director worries about
spiritual.high: a prayer life the director learns from

intellectual.high: the best student in his year

pastoral.low: a summer the pastor would not repeat
pastoral.middling: a summer the pastor was glad of
pastoral.high: a summer the parish still talks about

ordination: The cathedral is full for the first time since Easter. {man} lies on the floor for the litany and stands up a priest of {see}, and his mother, who has waited six years, does not sit down for the rest of the Mass.

{man} is ordained at the cathedral on a Saturday in June, with every priest of the diocese in the sanctuary who could drive, and his first blessing is for the bishop, which is the custom, and which you kneel for.
left: {man} has left the seminary in his {year} year: a letter to the rector, a letter to you, no reason given that the letters could hold. He will be a good husband to someone.
{man} did not come back after the summer. The rector says he saw it coming and could not say so; the vocations director says he did not. The parish that sent him takes it hard.
